title: Sameeksha's empty floor
description: An empty rectangular floor marked 12 ft by 16 ft with one teal square tile marked with a question mark beside it.

title: Must fit both sides
description: A 3 ft tile fits 4 times along 12 ft but leaves a 1 ft gap after 5 tiles along 16 ft.

title: Common factors of 12 and 16
description: A Venn diagram with factors of 12 and of 16; the overlap holds 1, 2 and 4, with 4 ringed as the largest.

title: The HCF tiles the room
description: A 16 ft by 12 ft room covered by 12 teal square tiles in 3 rows of 4, one tile marked 4 ft, with the HCF caption.

title: List, circle, choose
description: Factor chips for 10 and for 15 with 1 and 5 circled in both rows and 5 highlighted, captioned HCF = 5.

title: Rice into equal bags
description: 84 kg of rice packed into 7 teal bags and 108 kg into 9 amber bags, every bag 12 kg.

title: Test each bag weight
description: A test table for bag weights 5, 6 and 9 kg against 18 kg and 30 kg, where only 6 kg gets two ticks.

title: Which jump lands on both?
description: Two number lines to 18: jumps of 4 land on 12 but miss 18, while jumps of 6 land on both 12 and 18.

title: Longest jump equals HCF
description: A number line from 0 to 50 with five jumps of 10 landing on treasures at 30 and 50, captioned longest jump = HCF = 10.

title: From factors to the jump
description: Factor chips for 9 and 15 with 3 highlighted, and a number line to 15 with five jumps of 3 landing on 9 and 15.

title: Prime or composite?
description: Seven teal dots in a single row labelled prime beside six amber dots in 2 rows of 3 labelled composite.

title: Sorting numbers by factors
description: Three trays labelled Prime, Composite and Neither holding 2 and 13, then 9 and 15 with their factors, then 1.

title: Two routes, same primes
description: Two factor trees for 90, one starting 3 × 30 and one starting 2 × 45, both ending in the primes 2, 3, 3 and 5.

title: The division method
description: A division ladder for 105: 3 beside 105, 5 beside 35, then 7 circled, giving 105 = 3 × 5 × 7.

title: Divide, stop, check
description: Three panels: a division ladder for 60, the stopping prime 5 circled, and the check 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 60.

title: Two groups make a factor pair
description: The primes of 840 split into a teal group 2, 2, 7 making 28 and an amber group 2, 3, 5 making 30, with 840 = 28 × 30 below.

title: Factors of 225 from primes
description: Prime tiles 3, 3, 5, 5 above a table of products taken one to four at a time, ending in the list of the 9 factors of 225.

title: Bigger number, shorter list
description: Six tiles for 96 (five 2s and a 3) above two tiles for 121 (11 and 11), labelled as a counterexample.

title: Check with factor pairs
description: The factors 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18 in a row with three arcs pairing 1 with 18, 2 with 9 and 3 with 6.

topic_name: HCF from Common Subparts of Primes
title: Shared primes of 45 and 75
description: A Venn diagram with 3 only in 45, 3 and 5 shared, and 5 only in 75, above HCF = 3 × 5 = 15.

topic_name: HCF from Common Subparts of Primes
title: Matching primes of 112 and 84
description: Prime tiles of 112 above prime tiles of 84, with two 2s and the 7 linked, giving common factors 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28 and HCF 28.

topic_name: HCF from Common Subparts of Primes
title: Nothing shared but 1
description: Two separate circles, 96 with primes 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3 and 275 with primes 5, 5, 11, with HCF = 1 and co-prime below.

topic_name: HCF from Common Subparts of Primes
title: HCF in three steps
description: Three panels: 28 and 42 factorised, common subparts 2, 7 and 2 × 7, and HCF = 14.

topic_name: HCF by Taking the Minimum of Each Prime
title: Take the smaller count
description: A table counting 2s and 3s in 30 and 72, with a minimum row of 1 and 1, giving HCF = 2 × 3 = 6.

topic_name: HCF by Taking the Minimum of Each Prime
title: Line up the matching primes
description: Prime tiles for 225 and 750 lined up in columns; one 3 and two 5s are matched in both rows, giving HCF = 3 × 5 × 5 = 75.

topic_name: HCF by Taking the Minimum of Each Prime
title: HCF by minimum counts
description: Three panels for 36, 60 and 84: keep primes 2 and 3 and strike out 5 and 7, take 2 twice and 3 once, and HCF = 2 × 2 × 3 = 12.

title: Two torans, same length
description: Anshu's toran of four 6 cm strips and Guna's toran of three 8 cm strips both end at the same dashed line marked 24 cm.

title: Common multiples never stop
description: A number line with common multiples 24, 48, 72 and 96 joined by +24 jumps, 24 marked LCM, and an arrow showing the list goes on for ever.

title: Two rulers, first match
description: Two aligned rulers, one with marks every 4 and one with marks every 10, meet first at 20, circled as LCM = 20, and again at 40.

title: When the visits meet
description: A day line from 0 to 70 with ten 7 day hops above and seven 10 day hops below, both landing together on Day 70 at a sweet box.

title: Idli, vada, idli-vada
description: Number tiles 1 to 12 with 3, 6 and 9 teal for idli, 4 and 8 amber for vada, and 12 reddish purple for idli-vada, labelled LCM = 12.

title: First shared day
description: Two lists, 6, 12, 18 and 9, 18, with 18 circled in both and joined, and the line First shared day = LCM = 18.

title: Holds both factorisations
description: A Venn diagram with 2 in the 14 circle, 7 in the overlap and 5 in the 35 circle, and below it LCM = 2 × 5 × 7 = 70.

title: Take the taller stack
description: Stacks of squares for the 2s, 3s and 5s of 96 and 360, with the taller stack of each outlined, giving LCM = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 1440.

title: Both numbers fit inside
description: Prime tiles 2, 2, 3, 3 with a bracket over 2, 2, 3 for 12 and a bracket under 2, 3, 3 for 18, LCM = 36, checked by 36 ÷ 12 = 3 and 36 ÷ 18 = 2.

title: One number fits the other
labels: HCF of n and 5n is n
description: A bar of 6 above a bar of 18 split into three blocks of 6, with captions HCF of 6 and 18 is 6 and HCF of n and 5n is n.

title: The gap decides the HCF
labels: A common factor must divide the gap.
description: A number line from 8 to 13 with arcs joining 8 and 10 (HCF 2), 9 and 11 (HCF 1) and 12 and 13 (HCF 1).

title: Try, notice, explain
description: Three panels: three pairs of multiples of 5 with their HCFs, the pattern that the HCF is a multiple of 5, and the reason that 5 divides both.

title: Doubling doubles the HCF
description: 12 and 18 factorised with HCF 6, an arrow down, then 24 and 36 factorised with the extra 2 circled and HCF 12.

title: More than the multiplier
description: 84 shown as blocks 14, 3, 2 and 126 as blocks 14, 3, 3, with the shared 3 linked, and HCF = 14 × 3 = 42.

title: When is the HCF the multiplier?
description: Two panels: 6 × 4 and 6 × 5 with HCF 6, and 6 × 4 and 6 × 10 with HCF 6 × 2 = 12.

title: The division ladder for the HCF
description: A division ladder 84, 180 to 42, 90 to 21, 45 to 7, 15 with divisors 2, 2, 3 circled and HCF = 12.

title: The L gives the LCM
description: A division ladder for 630 and 770 ending in 9 and 11, with an L shape around 2, 5, 7 and 9, 11, and LCM = 6930.

title: One big step instead of three
description: A short ladder 300, 150 divided by 50 to 6, 3 and by 3 to 2, 1, with the note 50 = 2 × 5 × 5 and HCF = 150.

title: Ladder recap: HCF and LCM
description: A ladder dividing 36 and 48 by 12 to get 3 and 4, with arrows to HCF = 12 and LCM = 12 × 3 × 4 = 144.

title: The product is a common multiple
description: A number line from 0 to 48 with multiples of 6 above and of 8 below, meeting at 24 (the LCM) and 48 (the product).

title: HCF × LCM = Product
description: The prime tiles 3, 5, 7, 19 and 5 of 105 × 95 = 9975, with the first four braced as LCM 1995 and the last 5 ringed as HCF 5.

title: Every prime is shared out
description: 12 and 18 as prime tiles, shared out into an HCF box with 2, 3 and an LCM box with 2, 2, 3, 3, and 6 × 36 = 216 = 12 × 18.

title: Balance the product rule
description: A level balance with HCF 4 and LCM 24 on one pan and 8 and 12 on the other, above 4 × 24 = 96 = 8 × 12.

topic_name: Applying HCF and LCM, Part One
title: Split or meet?
description: Left, ribbons of 24 m and 36 m cut into 12 m pieces under Split: HCF; right, a number line where steps of 12 and 18 meet at 36 under Meet: LCM.

topic_name: Applying HCF and LCM, Part One
title: Primes in a Venn diagram
description: A Venn diagram of the primes of 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 and 2 × 3 × 3 × 7 with 2 and 3 in the overlap, giving HCF 6 and LCM 1260.

topic_name: Applying HCF and LCM, Part One
title: Which one does the story need?
description: A fork from Read the story to Equal parts, no leftovers with an HCF badge and to Meets again with an LCM badge.

topic_name: Applying HCF and LCM, Part Two
title: Hop along the multiples of 30
description: A number line hopping 0, 30, 60, with 30 = 7 × 4 + 2 crossed out and 60 = 7 × 8 + 4 ticked and ringed.

topic_name: Applying HCF and LCM, Part Two
title: Twelfths make adding easy
description: Three 12 cell bars: 2 teal cells for 1/6, 3 amber cells for 1/4, and 5 cells for the sum 5/12.

topic_name: Applying HCF and LCM, Part Two
title: Three story types, three moves
labels: Divisible by all: use the LCM
description: Three cards: Divisible by all, use the LCM; Chase, head start ÷ gain; Fractions, LCM of denominators.

topic_name: Chapter Review: HCF, LCM and Their Methods
title: Pick the method, then check
description: Three cards for List, Prime factors and Division ladder, with a green check strip HCF 14 × LCM 210 = 42 × 70.

topic_name: Chapter Review: HCF, LCM and Their Methods
title: Three quick cases
description: Three panels: 8 and 15 apart give HCF 1, LCM 120; 7 inside 21 gives HCF 7, LCM 21; 12 and 13 apart give HCF 1, LCM 156.

topic_name: Chapter Review: HCF, LCM and Their Methods
title: Four steps for any question
description: Four boxes in a row, Read, HCF or LCM?, Pick a method, Check, joined by arrows.

title: Rings that show primes
description: Rings around 2 (teal), 3 (amber), 6 (teal and amber halves) and 12 (two teal thirds and one amber third).

title: Decode and draw a ring
description: A key of 2 teal, 3 amber, 5 green, rings for 8 (three teal arcs) and 10 (teal and green), and an empty dashed ring for 15 with a question mark.

title: Fewest for HCF, most for LCM
description: 12 and 16 as primes, arrows to HCF 2 × 2 = 4 with a 3 by 4 grid of 4 ft tiles, and LCM 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 48.
